appearance_facts.fact: The chart is a line graph titled 'Agriculture vs Industry' with a horizontal 'Year' axis and two vertical percentage axes.
A solid blue line with circular markers connects data points from before 2010 through 2019; its 2014 point is visibly higher than its 2012 and 2015 points.
A dashed red line with square markers connects data points across the same year range; its 2014 point is visibly lower than its 2012 point and higher than its 2015 point.
At the 2014 position on the x-axis, the blue circular marker is positioned higher on the plot than the red square marker.
The left y-axis is labeled 'Agriculture (%)' in blue text, and the right y-axis is labeled 'Industry (%)' in red text.
Three percentage labels are printed on the chart: '16.85%' near a blue point around 2012, '29.4%' near a red point around 2012, and '16.36%' near a blue point around 2016.
The blue point at 2014 has no adjacent printed percentage label.
The red point at 2014 has no adjacent printed percentage label.

printed_facts.fact: The x-axis is labeled 'Year' with visible tick labels '2010', '2012', '2014', '2016', and '2018'.
The text '16.85%' is printed next to a blue circular marker located between the 2012 and 2014 tick marks.
The text '29.4%' is printed next to a red square marker located at the 2012 tick mark.
The text '16.36%' is printed next to a blue circular marker located at the 2016 tick mark.
The text '26.62%' is printed next to a red square marker located at the 2016 tick mark.

public_definitions: The goal is to compare the 2014 sector share percentage for Agriculture and Industry using the dashboard, then open the follow-up record for the sector with the larger 2014 percentage.
The routing criterion is the 'Larger 2014 sector share percentage shown in the dashboard'.
The program area is 'Economic sector share statistics'.
uncertain: The specific percentage values for the 2014 Agriculture and Industry data points are not printed on the chart.
The chart uses two separate y-axes (left for Agriculture, right for Industry) without visible numeric tick values, making direct numerical comparison from the image alone ambiguous.
